facts: Python is an interpreted, high-level, general-purpose programming language created by Guido van Rossum in 1991.
Python uses indentation to define code blocks instead of curly braces.
Python supports multiple programming paradigms: procedural, object-oriented, and functional.
Key built-in data structures include lists, tuples, sets, and dictionaries.
Python's package manager is pip, and the standard library is extensive.
Popular frameworks: Django and Flask for web, NumPy and Pandas for data science, FastAPI for APIs.
JavaScript is a lightweight, interpreted scripting language primarily used for web development.
JavaScript runs in the browser and on the server (via Node.js).
It is single-threaded but uses an event loop to handle asynchronous operations.
Key concepts: closures, prototypal inheritance, promises, async/await.
Popular frameworks: React, Vue, Angular for frontend; Express for backend.
ECMAScript is the standard that JavaScript is based on; ES6 (2015) introduced major improvements.
Machine learning is a subset of AI where systems learn patterns from data without explicit programming.
Main types: supervised learning (labeled data), unsupervised learning (unlabeled data), reinforcement learning.
Common algorithms: linear regression, decision trees, random forests, neural networks, SVMs.
Overfitting occurs when a model learns training data too well and fails to generalize.
Key libraries: scikit-learn, TensorFlow, PyTorch, Keras.
Training, validation, and test sets are used to build and evaluate models.
World War I (1914–1918) was triggered by the assassination of Archduke Franz Ferdinand.
World War II (1939–1945) ended with the surrender of Germany and Japan.
The Industrial Revolution began in Britain in the late 18th century, transforming economies worldwide.
The Cold War (1947–1991) was a geopolitical tension between the USA and USSR.
The Roman Empire at its height controlled much of Europe, North Africa, and the Middle East.
The Renaissance (14th–17th century) was a cultural rebirth of art, science, and philosophy in Europe.
The speed of light in a vacuum is approximately 299,792,458 meters per second.
DNA (deoxyribonucleic acid) carries genetic information in all living organisms.
Newton's three laws of motion describe the relationship between force and motion.
The periodic table organizes elements by atomic number and chemical properties.
Photosynthesis converts light energy into chemical energy stored as glucose in plants.
Einstein's theory of relativity states that E = mc², energy equals mass times the speed of light squared.
The Pythagorean theorem states: in a right triangle, a² + b² = c².
Pi (π) is an irrational number approximately equal to 3.14159.
Calculus was independently developed by Newton and Leibniz in the 17th century.
Prime numbers are integers greater than 1 divisible only by 1 and themselves.
The Fibonacci sequence: each number is the sum of the two preceding ones (0, 1, 1, 2, 3, 5, 8...).
Probability ranges from 0 (impossible) to 1 (certain).
Earth has 7 continents: Africa, Antarctica, Asia, Australia, Europe, North America, South America.
The Amazon River in South America carries more water than any other river on Earth.
Mount Everest, at 8,849 meters, is the highest point on Earth.
The Sahara Desert in Africa is the world's largest hot desert.
There are 195 countries in the world as recognized by the United Nations.
The Pacific Ocean is the largest and deepest ocean, covering more than 30% of Earth's surface.
The Milky Way galaxy contains an estimated 100–400 billion stars.
Light from the Sun takes approximately 8 minutes and 20 seconds to reach Earth.
The Big Bang theory describes the origin of the universe approximately 13.8 billion years ago.
A black hole is a region of spacetime where gravity is so strong that nothing can escape it.
Mars has the largest volcano in the solar system: Olympus Mons.
NASA's Apollo 11 mission landed the first humans on the Moon on July 20, 1969.
The Great Wall of China stretches over 13,000 miles and was built over many centuries.
The human body has 206 bones in adulthood.
Shakespeare wrote 37 plays and 154 sonnets.
The Internet was invented in the late 1960s as ARPANET by the US Department of Defense.
The Eiffel Tower was built in Paris in 1889 for the World's Fair.
Chess originated in India around the 6th century AD.
